key_insight: A unified analytical framework can diagnose and compare all major loss channels in photoelectrochemical cells, turning experimental I–V data into actionable design guidance for both BIJ and SEJ devices.
engineering_relevance: The model helps engineers pinpoint bottlenecks such as optical, recombination, thermodynamic, and interfacial losses, then translate them into optimization choices like better catalysts, nanostructuring, or improved semiconductor-electrolyte matching.
method: Uses a physically meaningful unified loss model for both built-in junction and semiconductor-electrolyte junction photoelectrodes
Generates current-voltage curves, efficiency metrics, and efficiency maps under ideal and real conditions
Fits experimental I–V data to decompose energy losses and visualize energy flow with Sankey diagrams
evidence_signal: The framework is validated against literature results across solar water splitting, CO2 reduction, NH3 synthesis, and solar redox flow batteries.
watch_item: Because the approach depends on fitting experimental I–V data, accuracy may be limited by measurement quality and by how well the chosen loss parameters capture complex real-device behavior.
paper_title: From Loss Diagnosis to Rational Design: A Unified Analytical Model for Photoelectrochemical Cells
